harmonicFunction: Am (i) - The melancholic emotional tonic establishing the song's tender vulnerability
F (VI) - The grand major submediant providing cinematic orchestral weight
Dm (iv) - Deepens the minor sentiment before resolving back to F
C (III / Tonic Major) - Triumphant release into the relative major in the chorus

techniques.name: Dramatic Stop-Time Dynamics & Acoustic/Electric Strumming
techniques.description: Strumming resonant open chords that cut off dead with absolute silence on dramatic pause cues before re-entering powerfully on the downbeat.

notes: Stop-time pauses: Sudden silence on beat 1 during the orchestral string hits
Subtle clean electric arpeggio fills behind the acoustic strumming
sequence: Strum the Am chord with steady, relaxed quarter notes
Transition to F and allow the open strings to ring
Execute the sudden stop-time choke: cut all string vibration instantly with your palms
Swell into the chorus on C major
tips: Acoustic guitar provides the warm organic bed; electric guitar adds shimmer with subtle chorus and reverb
The silence during the stop-time pauses must be 100% quiet—no lingering finger buzz
Kirk Pengilly played the iconic saxophone solo live, while guitars hold the heavy C - F foundation

techniques.name: Soulful Vocal-Range Lead Phrasing & Wide Vibrato
techniques.description: Transcribing Kirk Pengilly's legendary, soaring alto saxophone solo for electric guitar, using 8th-to-12th position C major pentatonic target tones, vocal-like whole-step bends, and sustained wide vibrato.

notes: C major pentatonic / A minor pentatonic positions across frets 8 to 13
Whole-step bend on fret 10 string 1 (D up to E)
Slow, singing vibrato emulating human vocal and saxophone breath control
Warm overdriven tube tone with long sustain and large hall reverb
sequence: Ascend from fret 8 on the B string through fret 10 and 12 on the high E
Bend fret 10 up to E, holding pitch steadily before a controlled release
Arc into fret 13 (high F) landing right on the chord shift to F major
Conclude on the tonic C note at the 8th fret of the B string with shimmering vibrato
tips: Use the neck pickup on a Stratocaster or Les Paul for that round, woody, saxophone-like warmth
Support your fretting fingers for precise pitch control on the 10th-fret whole-step bends
Add generous plate or hall reverb and subtle tape echo to recreate the cinematic Vienna video vibe

sections.name: Intro Orchestral Swell & Acoustic Entry
sections.description: The haunting cinematic opening where synthesized orchestral strings give way to the warm, solemn acoustic strumming of Am and F.
notes: Warm acoustic strumming with light pick attack
Let the bass notes ring clearly on downbeats
Establish the solemn 96 BPM tempo

sections.name: Verse 1 Cinematic Storytelling & Stop-Time
sections.description: Michael Hutchence's intimate narrative delivery punctuated by sudden, dramatic full-band silences on the orchestral hits.
notes: Warm, steady acoustic strumming
Kill all string sound instantly with fretting and pick palms on the stop cues
Re-enter firmly on the downbeat with zero hesitation

sections.name: Chorus 1 Soulful Anthem ('I Was Standing')
sections.description: The uplifting shift into the relative major C supporting Michael Hutchence's iconic vocal climax 'I was standing, you were there'.
notes: Broad, resonant open chord strumming with maximum projection
Accentuate beats 2 and 4
Let open strings ring naturally between C and F voicings

sections.name: Verse 2 Stratocaster Arpeggio Layering
sections.description: Deepening the arrangement behind the second verse with delicate, chorused Stratocaster arpeggio picking over the acoustic rhythm bed.
notes: Clean single-coil neck pickup with stereo chorus
Pick cleanly across strings 2, 3, 4, and 5
Mute cleanly on the stop-time pauses

sections.name: Kirk Pengilly Saxophone Solo (Guitar Arrangement)
sections.description: The unforgettable, soaring saxophone solo arranged note-for-note for electric guitar in 8th-to-12th position with crying bends and rich vibrato.
notes: Warm neck pickup tone with singing overdrive
Careful whole-step bends on fret 10 of string 1 up to E
Expressive vibrato mimicking saxophone breath control

sections.name: Outro Chorus Climax & Orchestral Finale
sections.description: The emotional climax of the song where the chorus repeats endlessly beneath Hutchence's passionate vocal cries, leading to the grand final orchestral chord.
notes: Strum with maximum emotional intensity
Lock into John Farriss's heavy snare backbeat
Let the final chord ring until natural decay

beginner.title: Open Chords & Strumming
steps: Learn the fundamental chords: Am, Fmaj7 (or barre F), Dm, and C
Practice smooth transitions in quarter notes at 96 BPM
Strum the chorus progression (C - F - C - F)

intermediate.title: The Stop-Time Choke
steps: Master the sudden palm-mute cutoff on the stop-time pauses
Coordinate clean acoustic strumming with electric guitar shimmers
Play seamlessly through the verse and chorus transitions

advanced.title: Complete Arrangement & Dynamic Touch
steps: Incorporate subtle electric arpeggios over the acoustic rhythm bed
Capture the epic emotional dynamics of the studio recording
Perform live with total control over dramatic silence

commonMistakes: Letting open strings buzz or sustain during the stop-time pauses
Fumbling the F major barre chord transition from Am
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Open chord transitions (Am → F → Dm → C)
5 minutes: Stop-time palm muting drill with metronome
metronomeWork: Practice with metronome at 96 BPM, ensuring clean stops on beat 1 and re-entry on beat 1 of the next measure
